title: Machine-learning network analysis identifies a conserved cell-mechanics gene module
summary: Researchers combined transcriptomic profiles with single-cell mechanical measurements from mouse and human systems and used machine-learning-based discriminative network analysis to infer a conserved five-gene module associated with cell mechanical properties. In perturbation experiments, changing CAV1 expression by silencing or overexpression altered measured cell stiffness, providing experimental support for a selected marker’s role.
organization: Technische Universität Dresden, Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Researchers combined transcriptomic profiles with single-cell mechanical measurements from mouse and human systems and used machine-learning-based discriminative network analysis to infer a conserved five-gene module associated with cell mechanical properties.
evidence.unknown: Only CAV1 was experimentally tested as a selected target in the reported perturbation experiments; the other genes are candidate regulators. Experiments show changes in measured stiffness in specific cell models, not broad physiological or clinical effects. Paper’s eLife assessment notes further validation, especially of genes with previously unknown roles, would strengthen the network.
evidence.ai_role: PC-corr analyzed transcriptomic data linked to measured mechanical phenotypes to identify a conserved five-gene signature and prioritize candidate regulators; selected genes were computationally assessed across six validation datasets, and CAV1 was experimentally perturbed to test effects on cell mechanics.
